Subject: Acme: Performance SLO / SLA follow-up (latency measurement & remedies)

Hi Alex / Priya  thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goals we heard:
- 95th percentile tail latency target of <= 250ms for our primary async text-generation route at 1k qps sustained.
- Support for streaming responses for long-form assistant flows (we discussed chunked streaming with < 100ms first-byte time).
- Concurrency requirement: support for 200 concurrent user sessions with bursts to 500 for short windows.

2) Questions we promised to confirm:
- Exactly how you measure latency today (client-side vs hop-to-hop).
- Any exclusions to the SLA you need (maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-side network issues).
- Preferred reporting cadence and what remedies (credits / retries / failover) are acceptable.

3) Next steps (proposed):
- I'll share a short SLO draft that defines measurement points, Exclusions section, and a 30/60/90 day reporting cadence. (attached)
- Can you confirm which IP ranges/networks will be allowed and whether you require dedicated capacity for peak windows?
- If the SLO language looks good, we can circle in Legal/Procurement and send a redline for the Master Services Agreement.

I've attached a first-pass SLO draft and a quick diagram for how we measure latency (client-first-byte vs server-generated). Please take a look and let me know what to adjust.

Thanks  talk soon.

--

Thanks Marissa  this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from our infra side: 

- Latency measurement: we measure 95p at the application layer (first byte received by our app from the service). That includes any network transit between our cloud VPC and the vendor but excludes client/browser rendering.
- Exclusions: we typically expect planned maintenance (with 72h notice) to be excluded, and any incidents caused by our misconfigured routing to be excluded as well.
- Remedies: our procurement team will want a credit table tied to monthly uptime/95p miss buckets. Typical ask is tiered credits (e.g., 5% credit if monthly 95p above target 1-2% of requests; 15% if >5%).

A couple of immediate questions on your draft: 
1) Your draft measures latency at "server egress"  can you add wording for equivalence to our app-layer measurement (first byte) and how you surface that in reports?
2) For streaming, what's your definition of first-byte time vs end-to-end? We need consistent language so SRE and procurement agree.

Happy to hop on a short call with Aditya/Rishi if needed.

 Alex
Alex Johnson
Platform Engineering Lead, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Alex  thanks for the details, very helpful. Quick answers inline and a suggested wording block you can share with Procurement/SRE: 

1) Measurement equivalence: We can measure "first-byte at server egress" and correlate it to your app-layer measurement. Suggested clause: 

"Latency will be measured as the time from receiving the request at Redwood's edge to the transmission of the first byte of the model response (server egress). For customers measuring at the application layer, Redwood will supply per-request timestamps (request receive, model first-byte, model last-byte) so the customer can compute equivalent app-layer latencies. Redwood's published 95th percentile SLOs will be computed on the server egress metric unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Streaming definition: 
- "First-byte time"  time from request to first response chunk.
- "End-to-end streaming"  time to final byte close.
- For SLA purposes we recommend: 95p first-byte <= 250ms, and 99p streaming-chunk interval <= 150ms for streaming-heavy routes.

3) Exclusions & remedies: We typically exclude: planned maintenance with >=72h notice, customer misconfiguration, and third-party upstream failures. Remedies: sample credit table included in attached SLO draft. We're happy to mirror Acme's credit structure if you share a preferred table  we can map to Redwood's monthly crediting.

4) Reporting cadence: Proposed: weekly dashboard during onboarding, then monthly SLO report with per-route 95/99 percentiles and an incident summary. We can export CSVs and raw per-request traces for spot checks.

Next step: Aditya/Rishi  can you confirm that Redwood's telemetry can export per-request timestamps and explain any sampling/aggregation that might affect exact percentile computation? If so, I'll update the draft clause and send a redline-ready SLO for Procurement.

Thanks  Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme: Performance SLO / SLA follow-up (latency measurement & remedies)

Looping in a quick technical note: 

- Telemetry: Redwood can export per-request timestamps: request_received_at, model_first_byte_at, model_last_byte_at, response_sent_at. These are available as logs (JSON lines) and can be pulled via our reporting API or S3 export.
- Aggregation/sampling: By default we compute percentiles on full data for customer-owned Dedicated deployments and on a 10% sample for shared/hosted during high-throughput windows. For contract language we recommend stating "percentiles computed on full request set for Dedicated; for hosted, percentiles computed on representative samples with sampling methodology provided on request."
- Concurrency: we use request queues and backpressure; for hard isolation we recommend Dedicated capacity (we can size based on your 200 concurrency baseline + 2.5x burst).

If Acme needs formal wording on sampling and compute, I can prepare a short paragraph to include in the SLO draft.

 Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
